Journal of Materials Chemistry A | ⭐ Review
💡 The novelty lies in systematically reviewing fabrication routes—from powder compaction to ultrathin membranes—for sulfide solid electrolytes, addressing the trade-off between thickness, ionic conductivity, and mechanical integrity. Its significance is guiding scalable processing of thin, continuous electrolyte layers that minimize inactive volume and resistance, enabling higher-energy all-solid-state batteries with intimate electrode contact and robust ion-conducting pathways.
